nri-world.title: Google Just Picked Its First Class of Junior Faculty Stars. One of Them Is Teaching Computers to Design Computer Chips.
nri-world.excerpt: Arizona State's Vidya Chhabria won an inaugural Google ML and Systems award and $100,000 in unrestricted funding — a spotlight on the diaspora's deepest and least-visible groove in American technology: the engineers who design the chips everyone else runs on.
nri-world.nri_angle: Chhabria's award redirects attention from the diaspora's celebrated tech executives to its foundational engineering layer — the Indian-origin researchers who have long populated electronic design automation and semiconductor labs, a lineage that now sits at the center of the world's most strategically contested technology.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Britain's Wealthiest Minority Just Told Its Politicians: We Are Done Being Taken for Granted
nri-world.excerpt: The British Indian Census 2025, presented at Parliament this month, finds a 1.8-million-strong community whose political loyalty is now genuinely up for grabs — and whose patience with being a 'tick-box exercise' has run out.
nri-world.image_caption: The Houses of Parliament and Big Ben in London
nri-world.nri_angle: For a community that measured success in incomes and degrees, the 2025 census marks a shift from being a statistic others quote to a constituency others must answer to — with loyalty leaking toward smaller parties and an unresolved question of belonging surfacing even at Parliament.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Man Tore an Indian Flag Outside a Texas City Hall. Six Members of Congress Decided It Was a Safety Story.
nri-world.excerpt: In Frisco, where one in three residents is now Asian, a viral act of contempt has forced the Indian American community to confront a question its success was supposed to settle: does it belong?
nri-world.nri_angle: The flag-tearing has shifted how Indian Americans talk about belonging — from offense to fear — and shows a maturing diaspora willing to push back publicly through its largest-ever congressional delegation rather than keep its head down.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Passed England as Australia's Largest Migrant Group. The Margin Was a Few Dozen People; the Trend Is Generational.
nri-world.excerpt: With 971,020 India-born residents and a median age two decades younger than the English-born population, the diaspora is no longer assimilating into Australia's story — it is helping write the next one.
nri-world.image_caption: Sydney, Australia; Indians have become the country's largest migrant group (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Becoming Australia's single largest migrant group means the Indian community is now a founding partner in what the country becomes — its weekend language schools, temples, and cricket leagues are the infrastructure of a population that expects to stay for generations.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: 'Grateful for Your Concern About the Diaspora': Modi and Carney Just Turned a Two-Year Freeze Into a Trade Ambition
nri-world.excerpt: Their fourth meeting in under a year targets a doubling of India-Canada trade by 2030 — but for 1.8 million Indo-Canadians, the real prize is the restoration of the visas and family ties a diplomatic collapse had frozen.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, official portrait
nri-world.nri_angle: The India-Canada thaw is, in practice, a diaspora deal: the trade talks center on talent mobility, education, and people-to-people ties, and a working diplomatic relationship means 1.8 million Indo-Canadians are no longer hostage to a single accusation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Cleared the Way for Banks to Pay NRIs More on Their Deposits — But Only Until September.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has temporarily scrapped the interest-rate ceilings on fresh FCNR(B) and longer-tenure NRE deposits through September 30, freeing banks to compete for overseas money as New Delhi scrambles to defend a battered rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian currency; the RBI has lifted rate caps on select NRI deposits until September 30 to attract overseas funds
markets-finance.nri_angle: This is one of the most directly actionable moves for NRIs all year: with rate caps lifted on FCNR(B) and long NRE deposits until September 30, banks are about to compete for diaspora dollars — meaning the rates Indians abroad earn on parked savings could jump, but only inside a closing window.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Made It Easier for NRIs to Buy Indian Stocks — RBI Opens a New Repatriable Rupee Account
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to let individuals living abroad open dedicated repatriable rupee accounts for investing in listed Indian shares, with sale proceeds free to be sent back overseas. A new 'Individual Foreign Investor' category streamlines the long-tangled plumbing of cross-border equity investment.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to ease how individuals abroad invest in listed Indian shares
markets-finance.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs want a stake in India's growth story but have long been deterred by a maze of account types, custodial rules and repatriation friction; this RBI amendment is aimed squarely at them, simplifying how a person abroad can buy Indian shares and — just as importantly — get their money back out.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold's Record Run Has Stalled. After a Blistering Two-Year Rally, the Fed Just Took the Wind Out of It.
markets-finance.excerpt: Bullion that surged 64% in 2025 — its best year in nearly five decades — has slid back below $4,400 an ounce, sinking to a seven-month low this month as a US-Iran peace deal, falling oil and a Federal Reserve hinting at rate hikes drain the fear that powered the climb. In India, prices have eased even as a steep new import duty bites.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold bullion bars; bullion's record rally has stalled as the Federal Reserve hints at rate hikes
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is not merely an asset for the Indian diaspora but a cultural reflex — the default store of value, the wedding gift, the hedge sent home — and after years of one-way gains, the metal's sudden wobble forces NRIs to reckon with whether they are buying a safe haven or chasing a peak that has already passed.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Largest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public. After a Decade of Delays, the NSE Just Filed Its IPO Papers.
markets-finance.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives platform — has filed draft papers for a pure offer-for-sale of up to 149 million shares worth roughly $3 billion, ending a listing saga that began in 2016 and handing long-waiting investors a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock exchange trading environment; India's NSE has filed draft papers for its long-delayed IPO
markets-finance.nri_angle: The NSE is the exchange where most of India's listed wealth changes hands — the very market NRIs tap through index funds, ETFs and direct holdings — and owning a slice of the bourse itself, alongside a record year of Indian mega-listings, gives the diaspora a rare chance to bet on the plumbing of India's markets rather than any single stock.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An India-US Trade Deal Is Suddenly Close. The US Trade Chief Visits This Month to Seal the First Tranche.
markets-finance.excerpt: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer travels to New Delhi on June 23-24 to put final touches on an interim agreement, with India's commerce minister signaling the first tranche could be done by mid-July. With a US-Iran truce cooling oil and the World Bank lifting its growth forecast, the macro backdrop has rarely looked better.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who said the first tranche of an India-US trade deal could be concluded by mid-July
markets-finance.nri_angle: An India-US trade pact sits at the center of the diaspora's two worlds — it shapes the export sectors and equities many NRIs invest in, the rupee that governs how far their remittances stretch, and the broader US-India relationship that frames diaspora life in America.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Defence Production Hits a Record ₹1.78 Lakh Crore — and the Stocks Riding the Boom Just Surged
markets-finance.excerpt: Government data shows India's annual defence output jumped 15.6 percent to an all-time high, with exports leaping 62 percent to nearly ₹38,500 crore and the private sector's share at a record. The Nifty India Defence index rose 3.9 percent as investors bet the 'Make in India' arms push has real momentum.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's defence production hit a record in FY26; the Nifty India Defence index surged 3.9 percent as exports jumped 62 percent
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's defence-manufacturing boom has become one of the most-watched investment themes for NRIs seeking exposure to the country's industrial rise — a story of self-reliance and export ambition that resonates with diaspora investors looking beyond IT and banks for the next structural growth story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Fed Just Stopped Promising Rate Cuts — and Started Hinting at a Hike. Warsh's First Meeting Spooked Wall Street.
markets-finance.excerpt: In Kevin Warsh's debut as Federal Reserve Chair, the central bank held rates at 3.50–3.75% but flipped its dot plot from an implied cut to an implied hike, sending US stocks sliding and the dollar firmer. For NRIs, a hawkish Fed reshapes everything from the rupee to mortgage rates to the calculus on sending money home.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Federal Reserve in Washington; the Fed held rates but flipped its projections toward a hike at Kevin Warsh's first meeting
markets-finance.nri_angle: A hawkish US Fed keeps the dollar strong and US mortgage and savings rates elevated — directly shaping how much NRIs earn on dollar deposits, what they pay on American home loans, and how many rupees their remittances buy back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Markets Just Logged Their Longest Winning Streak in Two Months. The Engine Is Cheaper Oil — and a Fragile Iran Deal.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty 50 closed above 24,000 for the first time in weeks as benchmarks rose for a fourth straight session, riding a near-three-month low in crude after a US-Iran peace deal promised to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. For NRIs, falling oil is rocket fuel for the rupee and the inflation outlook — but the truce is far from sealed.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; India's benchmarks logged their longest winning run in two months as oil eased
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs, this rally is a three-way win and a warning at once — cheaper oil eases India's import bill and supports the rupee that governs every remittance, while the fragility of the Iran truce means the gains rest on a deal that could still unravel.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: AI Fear Gutted India's IT Stocks by 27%. Now Some of the World's Biggest Investors Are Calling It a Bargain.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has been hammered as investors bet that artificial intelligence will hollow out India's software outsourcing giants. But with BlackRock and others arguing the market has been 'over-punished,' the very sector everyone is fleeing is starting to look like the contrarian call of 2026.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Tata Consultancy Services building; India's IT index has fallen about 27% in 2026 on AI-disruption fears
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's IT giants are the bedrock of countless NRI portfolios and the employers of a generation of diaspora engineers — so the question of whether AI is a death sentence or an overblown panic for TCS, Infosys and Wipro is both a financial and a deeply personal one for Indian software professionals abroad.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: After a Record $30 Billion Exodus, Foreign Money Is Edging Back Into India. The Tide May Be Turning.
markets-finance.excerpt: Foreign investors yanked a record $30.8 billion out of Indian equities in 2026 — then turned net buyers for the first time in 13 sessions as a US-Iran peace deal cooled oil and the RBI moved to steady the rupee. Wall Street firms now say India was 'over-punished,' and its absence from the AI trade may finally be an advantage.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock market display; foreign investors edged back into Indian equities this week
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs who watched Indian equities and their rupee-denominated portfolios slide through a brutal first half of 2026, the early signs of a foreign-money reversal reframe the question from 'how much more will I lose?' to whether the worst is now behind — and whether the diaspora's home-country bias is, for once, the contrarian call.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Biggest IPO Ever Is About to Land. Reliance Jio May File Draft Papers Within Days.
markets-finance.excerpt: Reliance Jio Infocomm could file draft papers for its expected $4 billion IPO within days — just before Mukesh Ambani's closely watched annual address on Friday — in what would be the first listing from his conglomerate in over two decades and potentially the largest public offering in Indian history.
markets-finance.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, whose Reliance Jio may file for India's largest-ever IPO within days
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio is the network most NRIs hand their relatives in India and the app bundle that powers their parents' digital lives; now the diaspora can weigh whether to own a slice of it — a decision sharpened by a record-breaking float that some veteran analysts warn has historically marked market tops.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Hit a Five-Week High and May Climb to 92. For NRIs Sending Money Home, the Window Is Closing.
markets-finance.excerpt: A US–Iran peace deal knocked oil prices to a three-month low and, stacked on the RBI's June measures to pull in dollars, sent the rupee surging for a third straight session to 94.56. One forecaster sees 92 per dollar by September. A stronger rupee is good news for India — but it means every dollar an NRI remits buys fewer rupees.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes; the currency hit a five-week high this week with forecasts of further gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: The rupee's direction is the single biggest variable in how much value an NRI's remittance or home-bound investment delivers — and with the currency now appreciating after months of weakness, the diaspora faces a narrowing window in which dollars still convert at favourable rates, a timing decision worth real money for anyone sending funds to family, servicing a loan, or funding property in India.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Is 18, She Beat the World No. 10 in Washington, and She Is India's Best Shot at an Olympic Squash Medal
sports.excerpt: Anahat Singh has cracked the world's top 20, defended her Indian Open title in Mumbai and become the youngest Asian woman ever to climb that high. With squash entering the Olympics for the first time at LA 2028, the teenager from Delhi is carrying a sport — and a diaspora — on her shoulders.
sports.image_caption: Indian squash great Joshna Chinappa, pictured after a junior title win — part of the generation that paved the way for teenage No. 1 Anahat Singh
sports.nri_angle: Squash is quietly one of the diaspora's sports — South Asian families fill racquet clubs in New Jersey, suburban London and the Greater Toronto Area — yet the community rarely sees itself represented at the elite level. Anahat Singh, 18, of Delhi, has cracked the world's top 20 (the youngest Asian woman ever to do so), beaten the world No. 10, and become India's best hope for a medal when squash debuts at the LA 2028 Olympics. A composed, fearless role model for NRI families and their daughters.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Is 21, She Is From Hyderabad, and She Just Broke a World Record on the Germans' Home Range
sports.excerpt: At the ISSF World Cup in Munich, Esha Singh shot 43 out of 50 to win the women's 25m pistol gold — a score that now stands as both the senior and junior world record. She beat the reigning Olympic champion and a former world champion to do it. India's quiet shooting empire just got a new face.
sports.image_caption: Indian pistol shooter Esha Singh, who set senior and junior 25m pistol world records (43/50) to win gold at the 2026 ISSF World Cup in Munich
sports.nri_angle: Shooting rarely makes the diaspora highlight reels that cricket and chess command, yet it has quietly become one of India's most reliable medal factories — a discipline where Indian women routinely beat established European and East Asian powers on their home ranges. Esha Singh, 21, from Hyderabad, outshot the reigning Olympic champion and a former world champion in Munich to set senior and junior world records, a quieter, more precise kind of pride for NRIs to follow.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Coached at MIT, Then the Grizzlies. Now Sonia Raman Is the First Indian-Origin Head Coach in the WNBA — and the Hardest Part Has Only Just Begun.
sports.excerpt: A walk-on guard who became a lawyer, then the winningest coach in MIT history, then the first Indian-American woman on an NBA bench, Raman took over the Seattle Storm this season. At 3-12, the rebuild is brutal — but the barrier she broke is permanent.
sports.image_caption: Seattle Storm guard Flau'jae Johnson during the 2026 WNBA season, Sonia Raman's first as head coach
sports.nri_angle: Sonia Raman is the first person of Indian origin to be a head coach in the WNBA — and earlier was the first Indian-American woman to coach in the NBA — a barrier-breaking career that offers South Asian families in America a powerful counter-example to the idea that professional sport is not a serious path.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A Son of Kerala Is About to Make World Cup History — in Qatar's Colours
sports.excerpt: Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid, the Doha-born winger with roots in Kannur, stands on the brink of becoming the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup.
sports.image_caption: The Qatar national football team, which 20-year-old Kerala-origin winger Tahsin Jamshid represents at the 2026 World Cup
sports.nri_angle: For decades, football-obsessed Kerala has poured its passion into supporting Brazil, Argentina and Germany at the World Cup without ever having a player of its own on the stage. Tahsin Jamshid — born in Doha to Malayali parents from Kannur — is poised to become the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup, a landmark for the Gulf's vast Malayali expatriate community and a bittersweet milestone for an India whose own men's team has never qualified.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: America's Cricket League Begins Its Fourth Season Tonight. It Was Built in the Suburbs the Diaspora Calls Home.
sports.excerpt: Major League Cricket returns June 18 with Steve Smith, Glenn Maxwell and Faf du Plessis on the marquee — but the league's real project is the American-raised, largely Indian-origin core now sharing a dressing room with them. From Grand Prairie to a sold-out Oakland Coliseum final, this is the diaspora's home team.
sports.image_caption: Grand Prairie Stadium in Texas, a purpose-built home of Major League Cricket
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket is the diaspora's own professional league — funded largely by Indian-American capital, staged in the U.S. suburbs with the densest South Asian populations, and increasingly powered by American-raised, mostly Indian-origin players like Monank Patel and Saurabh Netravalkar, turning a game of cultural preservation into a credible profession for immigrant kids.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Beat Carlsen Twice and the World Champion Once. In Oslo, a 20-Year-Old From Chennai Showed Why India Now Runs Chess.
sports.excerpt: R Praggnanandhaa's Norway Chess title is the latest sign of a generational shift: a country that had one world champion in 2013 now has the reigning world champion, the tournament's winner, and a clutch of 2700-rated players barely out of their teens. For a global game increasingly played in Indian living rooms, the future has an accent.
sports.image_caption: R Praggnanandhaa, who won Norway Chess 2026 ahead of Magnus Carlsen and world champion Gukesh Dommaraju
sports.nri_angle: India's chess surge runs straight through diaspora living rooms — the same low-cost, high-prestige game that Indian-American and Indian-British families have embraced en masse is now producing the world's most exciting young grandmasters, making players like Praggnanandhaa and Gukesh proof of concept for a particular immigrant bet.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two Indian Teenagers Are One Win From a Wimbledon Junior Main Draw. A Decade Ago, This Was Unthinkable.
sports.excerpt: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, seeded No. 1 in girls' qualifying, and 17-year-old Hitesh Chauhan both reached the final qualifying round at Roehampton — backed by academy training and corporate money that earlier generations never had.
sports.image_caption: The National Tennis Centre at Roehampton, the venue where Wimbledon junior qualifying is played

IndianSportsHub — Wimbledon Qualifiers: Maaya Rajeshwaran Headlines India's Junior Contingent
Khelnow — Maaya Rajeshwaran wins US Open 2025 opening match; Hitesh Chauhan bows out
ITF Tennis — Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi player profile

sports.nri_angle: The junior tennis pipeline India's rising players climb runs through the US college and ITF circuits where much of the diaspora lives, making these teenagers' breakthroughs personal and aspirational for Indian-American families.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: From a Bakersfield Muni to Shinnecock: The Gujarati-American Who Skipped Med School and Became the First IGPL Golfer at a Major
sports.excerpt: Manav Shah was supposed to be a doctor. Instead, the California-born son of Gujarati immigrants ground his way through Latin American mini-tours, rebuilt his game on an Indian circuit during a chance detour, and survived golf's toughest qualifier to reach the U.S. Open.
sports.image_caption: The first tee at Shinnecock Hills during the U.S. Open, where Manav Shah makes his Major debut
sports.nri_angle: Manav Shah is the immigrant-family story in miniature — a California-born son of Gujarati parents who chose golf over the expected path into medicine, kept his heritage alive through an Indian league, and now becomes the first IGPL golfer at a Major, a marker of how deep diaspora golf has grown.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Four Days After a Super Over Meltdown, India A Answered With 319 and a 101-Run Rout to Reach the Final
sports.excerpt: Three fifties — Tilak Varma's 59, plus 58 each from Priyansh Arya and Kumar Kushagra — and Nishant Sindhu's 4/31 carried India A into the tri-series final in Dambulla. It is the same A-team shop window that has been quietly minting India's senior internationals.
sports.image_caption: India A captain Tilak Varma, who top-scored with 59 as India A reached the tri-series final in Dambulla
sports.nri_angle: NRIs follow India's senior XI obsessively, but the A-team in Dambulla is where the next Gill or Jaiswal is being forged — the names on this team sheet are the players the diaspora will be watching for India over the next decade.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Same Week the Men Finished Last, India's Women Are Unbeaten in Auckland — and One Step From a Pro League Promotion
sports.excerpt: India's women's hockey team beat the USA 3-2 from two goals down, then edged Japan 2-1 to reach the FIH Nations Cup semi-finals with a game to spare. Win the tournament in New Zealand and they are promoted to the 2026-27 FIH Pro League — the elite circuit the men's side just endured a winless season in.
sports.image_caption: India captain Salima Tete, who scored against Japan as India reached the FIH Women's Nations Cup semi-finals in Auckland
sports.nri_angle: Hockey carries deep heritage for Indians abroad, and a Nations Cup win would promote India's women — led by athletes from Jharkhand's Simdega belt and the northeast — to the elite FIH Pro League, putting them on the same broadcast calendars the diaspora already follows for cricket and football.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Just Posted Their Highest-Ever World Cup Total. Mandhana and Shafali Took 11 Overs to Bury the Netherlands.
sports.excerpt: Smriti Mandhana (74 off 47) and Shafali Verma (55 off 38) shared a 115-run opening stand and brought up India's joint-fastest team fifty in Women's T20 World Cup history. India's 209 for 5 at Headingley was the most they have ever made at a World Cup — and a debutant Netherlands side never stood a chance.
sports.image_caption: Smriti Mandhana, who top-scored with 74 off 47 balls as India posted their highest-ever Women's T20 World Cup total
sports.nri_angle: India's women have never won a senior global title, and a generation of NRI families in Britain has watched them grow into genuine contenders — Headingley, in the heart of Yorkshire's South Asian community, drew a vocal, flag-waving diaspora crowd.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two Centuries, a 224-Run Stand, and India's 500th ODI Win: Gill and Kishan Sink Afghanistan in Lucknow
sports.excerpt: Shubman Gill's ninth ODI hundred and Ishan Kishan's maiden century carried India to a 15-run victory at Lucknow, sealing the three-match series 2-0 with a game to spare — and handing the country a landmark 500th win in one-day internationals.
sports.image_caption: Shubman Gill scored his ninth ODI century to lead India past Afghanistan in the second ODI at Lucknow
sports.nri_angle: India's white-ball rebuild under captain Shubman Gill is appointment viewing for the cricket-following Indian diaspora, and a milestone 500th ODI win, twin centuries, and a touch of old-fashioned sportsmanship make for exactly the kind of storyline NRIs forward to family group chats within minutes.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nikesh Arora Just Closed His Third Big Deal in a Year. He's Betting $30 Billion That AI Will Break Security as We Know It.
technology.excerpt: Palo Alto Networks completed its $3.35 billion buy of Chronosphere — the latest in a buying spree by the Indian American CEO who keeps putting his own money on the line.
technology.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks Chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt
technology.nri_angle: Palo Alto Networks is a major Bay Area employer of Indian engineers, and its Indian American CEO's aggressive AI-security strategy is a leading indicator for thousands of diaspora careers and portfolios.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Opendoor Is Shutting Its Entire India Operation. The Reason Isn't Cost — It's That AI Made the Work Disappear.
technology.excerpt: The real-estate platform is winding down its Chennai and Bengaluru offices, affecting 250 employees, and says the back-office work simply no longer needs to exist offshore.
technology.nri_angle: The wage-arbitrage offshoring model that built India's tech industry and funded a generation of NRI migration faces its first AI-driven existential test — reshaping the pipeline that brought the diaspora to America.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Washington Just Barred 'Foreign Nationals' From Anthropic's Best AI — Including the Indian Engineers Who Built It.
technology.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind US export order forced Anthropic to pull Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline worldwide, drawing a line straight through the diaspora's professional life.
technology.nri_angle: A huge share of frontier-AI-lab researchers are Indian nationals on visas — and a US order barring 'foreign nationals' from the top models puts the diaspora's dual identity at the center of a sovereignty fight.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Wipro Built a Whole Center to Run Claude. The Company That Sold Cheap Code Is Now Selling AI to Replace It.
technology.excerpt: The Bengaluru IT giant will certify 10,000 staff on Anthropic's models in 18 months — a defensive pivot that quietly redraws the career math for every Indian engineer who came up through the services pipeline.
technology.image_caption: Software engineers collaborating at a technology workspace, the kind of delivery floor Wipro is retraining around Anthropic's Claude models.
technology.nri_angle: For the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers — and their relatives in the US and UK — who climbed out of the IT services pipeline that Wipro built, the company's bet on Claude is a signal that the old ladder of 'learn to code, get placed, get an H-1B' is being rebuilt around AI fluency rather than headcount.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's First Real Chip Fab Just Signed the Hardest Vendor in Tech. Now the Hard Part Begins.
technology.excerpt: Tata Electronics has locked in ASML lithography for its $11 billion Dholera fab, with first chips due by December — a milestone that turns India's semiconductor talk into a delivery deadline.
technology.image_caption: A close-up of a semiconductor processor die, the class of analog and logic chips Tata's Dholera fab aims to produce.
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor engineers staff the design and process teams at Micron, Intel, AMD, Applied Materials and ASML's own customers — and a working fab in Gujarat is the first credible reason in a generation for some of them to consider building chips at home instead of abroad.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Biggest Exchange Finally Filed to Go Public. At $57 Billion, NRIs Are About to Get a Piece of the Casino's House.
technology.excerpt: After years of regulatory delay, the National Stock Exchange filed IPO papers this week — a once-blocked listing that hands a $2.6 billion windfall to early backers and a rare shot at owning the rails of India's markets.
technology.nri_angle: NRIs have spent years pouring money into Indian stocks through the NSE's platform; its long-delayed IPO is the first realistic chance for diaspora investors — increasingly able to buy in via GIFT City and global brokerages — to own the exchange itself rather than just trade on it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Qualcomm Is Betting $10 Billion That the Phone Era Is Over. The Data Center Is the New Battleground.
technology.excerpt: The chipmaker is in talks to buy Tenstorrent and its star engineer Jim Keller, days before an investor day meant to convince Wall Street it can challenge Nvidia. For the Indian engineers who staff its chip-design ranks, it's a whole new product line.
technology.image_caption: Qualcomm President and CEO Cristiano Amon, who is steering the company toward data-center and edge-AI silicon
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of Indian-origin chip engineers in the US and runs huge design centers in Bengaluru and Hyderabad; a pivot into data-center AI silicon reshapes the careers and job map for that workforce.

lifestyle-health.title: A Cheap Diabetes Drug Was Hailed as a Longevity Pill. A 21-Year Study Says Diet and Exercise Beat It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking adults with prediabetes for more than two decades, researchers found that an intensive diet-and-exercise program lowered the risk of piling up multiple chronic diseases — while metformin, the drug touted as an anti-ageing wonder, did no better than a placebo.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A diet rich in vegetables and regular exercise; a 21-year study found lifestyle change, not metformin, cut the risk of multiple chronic diseases
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop prediabetes and Type 2 diabetes earlier and at lower body weights than almost any other group, and metformin is one of the most prescribed drugs in Indian households worldwide — so the finding that a structured diet-and-exercise routine, not the pill, is what actually held off the cascade of chronic disease over 21 years speaks directly to how the NRI community should weight medication against daily habits.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Vitamin in Your Morning Orange May Help Keep Your Brain Younger, a Study of 2,000 Adults Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Japanese researchers measured vitamin C directly in the blood of older adults — not just their diets — and found that those with higher levels had better-preserved gray matter and stronger connections in a brain network central to memory.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Citrus fruit, a key vitamin C source; a study links higher blood vitamin C to better-preserved brain structure in older adults
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Vegetarian and plant-forward Indian diets are often rich in vitamin C from citrus, amla, guava, peppers and leafy greens — but the heavy boiling and long cooking common in desi kitchens destroys much of it, making this a rare case where a traditional diaspora strength can quietly become a deficiency that may matter for the ageing brain.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Eat More Plant Polyphenols and You May Hurt Less — New Research Links Diet to Migraine Relief
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study published this month in PLOS One found that people who ate more polyphenol-rich foods — berries, green tea, coffee, herbs and spices — reported lower pain sensitivity and less migraine-related disability. For a diaspora whose traditional kitchen is built on turmeric, ginger and green tea, the implications are quietly encouraging.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Green tea, berries and spices are rich in polyphenols; new research links higher polyphenol intake to lower pain sensitivity and migraine disability
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Migraine is strikingly common among South Asian women, and the polyphenols this study credits with easing pain — from turmeric and ginger to green tea and spices — are precisely the compounds that fill a traditional Indian kitchen, suggesting the diaspora may already hold a dietary lever it rarely thinks to pull.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Not All Vegetarian Diets Are Equal: A 400,000-Person Study Shows Why the Quality of Plant Foods Decides Your Health
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Pooling data from more than 407,000 adults across Europe and Britain, researchers found that a diet built on healthy plant foods sharply lowered the risk of developing both cancer and heart-and-metabolic disease together — while a plant-based diet heavy on refined grains, sugar and fried food did the opposite. The effect was strongest in adults under 60.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Lentils, vegetables and whole grains; a 400,000-person study shows the quality of plant foods, not the vegetarian label, decides health outcomes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora often equates 'vegetarian' with 'healthy' — yet a diet of white rice, fried snacks, sweets and refined flour is plant-based and harmful, while one of dal, vegetables and whole grains is plant-based and protective; this study draws exactly that line, and it matters enormously for a community already prone to diabetes and heart disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Bad Sleep in Your Forties and Fifties May Quietly Shape How You Feel a Decade Later — Especially for Women
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study presented at SLEEP 2026 tracked nearly 600 middle-aged and older adults for nine years and found that those who struggled to sleep ended up with lower psychological well-being years on. The link held firm for women but faded for men once other factors were stripped out.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person lying awake at night; a new study links midlife sleep problems to lower well-being a decade later, especially in women
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Sleep is the first thing to go for diaspora women juggling demanding careers, young children and ageing parents across time zones — and this research suggests the broken nights of midlife are not just an inconvenience but a long-term risk to how they will feel and function a decade from now.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cutting Out Sugar Entirely Sounds Healthy. A New Study Suggests It Can Backfire on Your Gut.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at Kuwait's Dasman Diabetes Institute fed mice a low-fat diet for 16 weeks — one group with table sugar, one with none at all. The completely sugar-free group did not gain weight, but developed disrupted gut bacteria, inflammation, insulin resistance and early signs of fatty liver.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: White sugar; a new study suggests cutting sucrose out entirely can disrupt gut health and metabolism
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora families are increasingly going 'sugar-free' to fight the community's high rates of diabetes — swapping out everything from chai sugar to sweets — yet this research is an early warning that the goal should be balance and moderation, not total elimination, especially for a population already prone to metabolic disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Found the Muscle Switch That Exercise Flips On. It May Explain Why Movement Keeps You Strong With Age.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A protein called NOX4 falls as we grow older and inactive — and when researchers stripped it from muscle, animals grew frail, lost muscle and developed insulin resistance. Exercise restored it, offering a molecular clue to why staying active protects the ageing body.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Strength training in older age; new research links the muscle protein NOX4 to how exercise preserves strength
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians lose muscle earlier and carry more body fat at the same weight than most populations, making age-related frailty and insulin resistance a quiet diaspora epidemic — and this research underlines that for the NRI parent or professional, regular movement is not optional but a biological necessity that flips on the body's own repair machinery.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It Is Not Just How High Your Blood Pressure Is. How Much It Swings May Quietly Age Your Brain.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Monash University study tracking blood pressure around the clock found that bigger 24-hour swings were tied to worse memory and problem-solving — a decline equivalent to roughly seven extra years of brain ageing — and to visible signs of injury on brain scans.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A blood pressure measurement; a new study links 24-hour swings in blood pressure to poorer brain health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Hypertension is rampant and frequently undertreated among South Asians, and most diaspora families judge it by a single clinic reading — yet this research suggests the hidden danger lies in the swings between readings, a pattern only round-the-clock monitoring can catch, reframing how NRIs should manage their own and their ageing parents' blood pressure.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be Just What's in Ultra-Processed Foods That Hurts You — It's How They're Made
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new Tufts University analysis of two decades of US health data found that people who ate more ultra-processed foods had worse health and a higher risk of early death — even after accounting for the nutrition inside the food. The processing itself, the researchers argue, may carry an independent harm.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Packaged ultra-processed foods; a Tufts analysis found their industrial processing may harm health independent of the nutrition they contain
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian and South Asian families increasingly lean on packaged namkeen, instant mixes, sugary biscuits and ready meals as life gets busier abroad — and this research suggests the industrial processing in those products may damage health in ways that reading the nutrition label alone will never reveal.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Most Addictive Foods Aren't Only the Sugary Ones. A New Study Points the Finger at Refined Starch.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers analyzing why ultra-processed foods are so hard to stop eating found that the usual villain — sugar — is only half the story. Rapidly digested refined carbohydrates, even in savory snacks with little or no added sugar, may be just as powerful a driver of cravings.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Savory snacks like potato chips and fried namkeen deliver rapidly digested refined starch that researchers link to hard-to-stop cravings
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian snacking culture is built on refined-flour and rapidly-digested treats — namkeen, sev, mathri, fried maida snacks and white-rice indulgences — and this research suggests these savory staples may hijack appetite as effectively as anything sweet, a blind spot for a community already prone to diabetes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Cheap Amino-Acid Supplement Plus Exercise Cut Older Adults' Fatigue Almost in Half, a Pilot Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a controlled study of obese older adults, those who paired eight weeks of exercise with branched-chain amino acids saw fatigue fall 45 percent and depressive symptoms drop — while the placebo group's tiredness nearly doubled. The findings hint at a low-cost way to help aging bodies recover from the very exercise meant to keep them strong.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Older adults exercising; a UT Health San Antonio pilot trial found branched-chain amino acids cut fatigue 45 percent when paired with exercise
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many diaspora families care for aging parents who eat largely vegetarian diets that can fall short on the leucine-rich protein that guards against age-related muscle loss — making an affordable amino-acid strategy especially relevant for South Asian elders at high risk of sarcopenia and frailty.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Bad Sleep May Do More Than Tire You Out — A Study of 1.8 Million People Links Insomnia to an Irregular Heartbeat
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In one of the largest analyses of its kind, Japanese researchers found that people with insomnia had a 14 percent higher chance of developing atrial fibrillation, the irregular heart rhythm that raises the risk of stroke. The link was strongest in women and in adults under 65.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 1.8 million people linked insomnia to a 14 percent higher risk of atrial fibrillation, with the strongest effect in women and adults under 65
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry a well-documented double burden of disrupted sleep and early heart disease, and diaspora life adds its own insomnia triggers — late-night calls across time zones, shift work and chronic stress — making the sleep-heart connection especially worth heeding for the community.

carousel.title: She Is 18, She Beat the World No. 10 in Washington, and She Is India's Best Shot at an Olympic Squash Medal
carousel.excerpt: Anahat Singh has cracked the world's top 20, defended her Indian Open title in Mumbai and become the youngest Asian woman ever to climb that high. With squash entering the Olympics for the first time at LA 2028, the teenager from Delhi is carrying a sport — and a diaspora — on her shoulders.
carousel.image_caption: Indian squash great Joshna Chinappa, pictured after a junior title win — part of the generation that paved the way for teenage No. 1 Anahat Singh
carousel.nri_angle: Squash is quietly one of the diaspora's sports — South Asian families fill racquet clubs in New Jersey, suburban London and the Greater Toronto Area — yet the community rarely sees itself represented at the elite level. Anahat Singh, 18, of Delhi, has cracked the world's top 20 (the youngest Asian woman ever to do so), beaten the world No. 10, and become India's best hope for a medal when squash debuts at the LA 2028 Olympics. A composed, fearless role model for NRI families and their daughters.

carousel.title: India Just Cleared the Way for Banks to Pay NRIs More on Their Deposits — But Only Until September.
carousel.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has temporarily scrapped the interest-rate ceilings on fresh FCNR(B) and longer-tenure NRE deposits through September 30, freeing banks to compete for overseas money as New Delhi scrambles to defend a battered rupee.
carousel.image_caption: Indian currency; the RBI has lifted rate caps on select NRI deposits until September 30 to attract overseas funds
carousel.nri_angle: This is one of the most directly actionable moves for NRIs all year: with rate caps lifted on FCNR(B) and long NRE deposits until September 30, banks are about to compete for diaspora dollars — meaning the rates Indians abroad earn on parked savings could jump, but only inside a closing window.
